title: fix(app-shell): the flow designer stops warning on a source node's own outputs on its out-edges; the Problems panel scan takes the connector registry (objectui#11085)
body:
Part of #11085
Clause-②: no

Two designer surfaces reported a guard reference as "not a reference in scope" although the engine writes it before it evaluates the guard. This PR completes site 2 (both surfaces) and lands the pure half of site 1. Site 1's host wiring is held back on purpose, see "Why Part of, not a full close" below.

## Site 2: an edge guard sees its source node's own outputs (complete)

- `inspectors/flow-scope.ts`: `edgeSourceOutputRefs(draft, edge, connectors)` is the one rule for which of the source node's own outputs are in scope on its out-edge: the source's `nodeOutputRefs`, except on a `fault` edge (the engine walks it only when the node failed, with nothing written back, and never evaluates its condition) and on an edge leaving the start node (it contributes the trigger record, the rule `resolveFlowScope` already applies). `resolveEdgeScope(draft, edge, locale, connectors)` is `resolveFlowScope` at the source plus those refs, de-duplicated by token.
- `inspectors/useFlowScope.ts`: `useEdgeScope(draft, edge, connectors)` is the React twin: `useFlowScope` at the source with `edgeSourceOutputRefs` as its `extraRefs`. The `useFlowScope` doc that told edge callers to pass the source id (the defect itself) now routes them to `useEdgeScope`.
- `inspectors/FlowEdgeInspector.tsx`: the guard's picker and its scope note read `useEdgeScope`.
- `previews/flow-expr-problems.ts`: the Problems panel's edge loop reads `resolveEdgeScope`.

## Site 1: the connector registry reaches the Problems panel's scan (pure half only)

- `flowExpressionProblems(draft, locale, connectors)` threads the registry into `resolveFlowScope` for nodes and `resolveEdgeScope` for edges.
- `buildFlowProblems` lives in `previews/flow-problems.ts` (the order placed it in `flow-expr-problems.ts`); it takes an optional `connectors` argument and passes it through.

## Why Part of, not a full close

The Problems panel's host, the only caller of `buildFlowProblems`, is `previews/FlowPreview.tsx`: its `problems` memo feeds the Problems panel, the canvas badges, the banner and the red error ring. The dispatch order bars that file (objectui#10862 slice 4 edits it in parallel) and says to stop and report if the host lives there, so the host edit is not made here. It is three lines, and adds nothing beyond this PR's seam:

1. import `useConnectorRegistry` from `../inspectors/connector-input-fields.js` and `hasCommittedConnectorAction` from `../inspectors/flow-scope.js`;
2. beside the `problems` memo: `const connectors = useConnectorRegistry(hasCommittedConnectorAction(d));`
3. pass `connectors` into the `buildFlowProblems({ ... })` call and add it to that memo's dependency list.

Until then a guard `post.ok == true` downstream of a committed connector action still draws the Problems-panel warning (the inspectors accept it since objectui#11084), and objectui#11085 stays open for that half.

## Engine premise, re-measured on objectstack origin/main `14f80e23`

- `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts`, `executeNode`: on success the step is logged, then the block commented "Write back output variables" sets `node.id + '.' + key` for every key of `result.output`, and only after it does `traverseNext` run.
- `get_record` writes its `outputVariable` inside its executor (`builtin/crud-nodes.ts`, `variables.set(outputVariable, record)`), before control returns to traversal.
- `traverseNext` selects out-edges with `e.type !== 'fault'`. On failure the engine sets `$error` and executes the `fault` edge's target directly: no condition evaluated, no output written back.

## Pins (per site: the reference the engine writes is clean, a reference no node writes still warns)

- `inspectors/flow-scope.test.ts`, describe "edge scope — the source node’s own outputs are in scope on its out-edges (objectui#11085)": `lead` joins the out-edge of a `get_record` with `outputVariable: lead` while the node scope is unchanged; a fault edge, a start-node edge and a missing source add none; `post.ok` joins a connector action's own out-edge only with the registry.
- `previews/flow-expr-problems.test.ts`, describe "flowExpressionProblems — references the engine writes (objectui#11085)": site 2 `lead.status == 'open'` clean on the out-edge, `ghost.status` still warns, the fault edge still warns; site 1 `post.ok == true` clean on a node, its own out-edge and a later edge with the registry, reported without it, `ghost.ok` reported with it.
- `previews/flow-problems.test.ts`, describe "buildFlowProblems — the connector registry reaches the expression scan (objectui#11085)".
- `inspectors/FlowEdgeInspector.sourceOutputs-11085.test.tsx`: through the real edge inspector wiring, no note for `lead.status`, a note for `ghost.status`, a note for `lead.status` on a fault edge.

Assertions read the verdict's level, target and named root, never the note's wording.

## Verification (all at HEAD `2be3ab1a2`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/`: 79 files, 1065 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/`: 114 files, 1583 passed, 1 skipped (a pre-existing `skipIf` in `flow-node-config.spec-reconciliation.test.ts`).
- The 22 test files that name a changed module or its consumers (`FlowPreview`, `FlowCanvas`, `ProblemsPanel`, `FlowInspector`, `spec-symbol-parity`): 434 passed.
- `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` exit 0, then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exit 0; `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists all four touched test files.
- eslint on the 9 changed TS files (`--format json`: 9 files): 0 errors, 2 warnings, both `no-explicit-any` on the pre-existing `(draft as any).edges` line of `FlowEdgeInspector.tsx`, a line this diff does not touch. Type-aware linting is not enabled in `eslint.config.js` (no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`), so this diff cannot move a lint verdict on an untouched file.
- `check-changeset-presence`, `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new), `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`: all exit 0. `check-changeset-claims` names three pending changesets that mention `flow-expr-problems.ts` / `flow-scope.ts`; each paragraph was re-read and none is falsified by this diff.

## Ablations (one-shot, objectstack `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` wrap mode; the tests import `src` by relative path, so no `dist` is on the resolution path)

1. `edgeSourceOutputRefs` returns none: 5 red (two flow-scope edge-scope pins, the scan's site-2 `lead.status` pin, the scan's site-1 own-edge `post.ok` assertion, the edge inspector's `lead.status` pin); every control stayed green. Restore proven: blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
2. `buildFlowProblems` drops `connectors`: 1 red (its registry pin). Restore proven.
3. `flowExpressionProblems` drops `connectors` from the node scope: 2 red (the scan's site-1 node pin and the `buildFlowProblems` registry pin). Restore proven.

## Declared narrowing

- Not run locally: the rest of `packages/app-shell` and the repo-wide farm, which are CI's. A whole `metadata-admin/` run (344 files) was started and stopped after 10 minutes without a verdict: NOT MEASURED, because it held the shared verify lock past the foreground cap while a sibling seat was parked behind it. `previews/` and `inspectors/` were run whole instead, plus the 22-file reader list; that list is a name grep, so a test reaching these modules only through a registry without naming them is outside it unless it sits in those two directories.

## Acceptance notes

- The file surface grew past the claim's list by two files, both forced: `previews/flow-problems.ts` (home of `buildFlowProblems`) and `inspectors/useFlowScope.ts` (its edge doc would have kept teaching the defect; `useEdgeScope` lives beside `useFlowScope`).
- Unmeasured observation, not filed: an out-edge of the START node resolves the start node's own scope, where trigger fields are bare (`status`), while downstream nodes read `record.status`. Whether the engine binds bare trigger fields when it evaluates the start node's out-edge guards was not measured here. The Problems panel skips those edges; only the edge inspector's picker offers the bare spelling. Carrier: none.
